Prior product OPENREP-SUPINTREP-0748 — Assess the cross-Strait military balance and PRC options for blockade or quarantine of Taiwan.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: No reporting addresses current cross-Strait military balance or blockade feasibility.

KEY JUDGEMENTS: Likely that PRC's military posture reflects routine readiness without specific blockade plans (focused on general deterrence).

Realistic possibility that the PRC could announce and enforce a maritime exclusion zone (i.e., a blockade) around Taiwan.

Realistic possibility that the PRC could use a blockade to coerce, intimidate, or put political pressure on Taiwan.

Realistic possibility that the PRC could use a blockade to facilitate the projection of PRC military presence and political influence further into the Western Pacific.

Realistic possibility that the PRC could use a blockade to help achieve a broader goal of becoming a regional hegemon in its part of Eurasia.

ASSESSMENT: Document 0 (C2) explicitly lists "announce and enforce a maritime exclusion zone (i.e., a blockade) around Taiwan" among objectives achievable through PRC domination of its near-seas region, establishing this as a stated PRC capability. Document 7 (B2) corroborates Taiwan's vulnerability by noting that "Taiwan's reliance on energy imports and limited stockpiling capacity may leave it vulnerable to supply disruptions, such as a PRC blockade," providing evidence of potential impact.

The same Document 0 frames PRC objectives around "control fishing operations, oil and gas exploration activities, seabed mining, and seabed internet cable-laying operations" and "coerce, intimidate, or put political pressure on other countries bordering on the SCS," suggesting economic and diplomatic tools may achieve PRC goals without the risks of military confrontation.
